input.query:
WITH RECURSIVE path(ind, start_id, transfer_id, links, trail) AS (
    SELECT indicator_id, transfer_id, transfer_id, 0, transfer_id FROM alert_contributions
    UNION ALL
    SELECT path.ind, path.start_id, o.debit_transfer_id, path.links + 1, path.trail || '>' || o.debit_transfer_id
    FROM path JOIN onward_links o ON o.credit_transfer_id = path.transfer_id
  )
  SELECT ind, start_id, trail, links, t.sender, t.receiver, NOT EXISTS (SELECT 1 FROM onward_links WHERE credit_transfer_id = path.transfer_id) AS ends
  FROM path JOIN transfers t ON t.transfer_id=path.transfer_id ORDER BY ind, start_id, links

findings.statement: Scope: one bounded replay (run:5ce89f521e5e, 50,000 dataset events, 3 of 3 jobs completed, clink exit status 0, not cancelled). Parameters: fan-in needs at least 5 distinct senders within a 3,600,000 ms event-time window, and an onward link needs a debit within 1,800,000 ms of a credit. The dataset contains 50,000 transfers, 12,072 accounts, 12,321 devices, 691 onward links and 6 fan-in alerts. Everything below holds only for this dataset as processed by this run.

fan_in:A-85921:1794855600000: account A-85921, window 1794855600000–1794859200000, 6 senders, 6 transfers, total 15000. Contributing transfers: T005750, T005789, T005830, T005868, T005934, T005978. Each of the six contributing transfers is for 2500.

A-10859 alert, candidate onward-transfer paths: the longest has 3 onward links. Path accounts are A-10859, A-78340, A-75793, A-85287 and A-92332. The paths branch at A-78340 and end at two accounts, A-92332 (via T011628) and A-85287 (via T011695). Neither has a further qualifying transfer in this dataset, and neither has a fan-in alert. Every contributing transfer starts at least one path, through T011583 and/or T011670 (A-10859 to A-78340).

A-20636 alert: the longest path has 1 onward link. Path accounts are A-20636 and A-36729. Five contributing transfers link to T033506 (A-20636 to A-36729), and all paths end at A-36729. Contributing transfer T033316 has no onward link, and T033506 has no further one.

A-28137 alert: none of its 7 contributing transfers has an onward link in this dataset. So it has no candidate onward-transfer paths (max depth 0), no end accounts, and A-28137 is its only path account.

A-37573 alert: the longest path has 4 onward links. Path accounts are A-37573, A-38045, A-93288, A-63022 and A-54215. There are two parallel candidate sequences over the same accounts: T003168>T003182>T003201>T003222 (linked from T003057, T003091, T003124, T003154) and T003391>T003416>T003433>T003454 (linked from T003248, T003287, T003319). Both end at A-54215, which has no further qualifying transfer in this dataset and no fan-in alert.

A-83577 alert: the longest path has 5 onward links, the most of any alert. Path accounts are A-83577, A-56768, A-83094, A-43725, A-14799 and A-39382. All 8 contributing transfers link to the single sequence T022572>T022592>T022609>T022629>T022649, which ends at A-39382. A-39382 has no further qualifying transfer in this dataset and no fan-in alert.

A-85921 alert: the longest path has 1 onward link. Path accounts are A-85921 and A-10758. Four contributing transfers link to T005888 (A-85921 to A-10758, 9500), and the paths end at A-10758. Contributing transfers T005934 and T005978 have no onward link.

Shared devices on paths. A-10859: device D-79802 was used to send by A-10859 and A-78340, which are the alerted account and its first onward account. A-37573: device D-45880 was used to send by A-37573, A-38045, A-93288 and A-63022, which are every path account that sent anything; all 8 onward transfers on its paths came from D-45880. A-83577: device D-40018 was used to send by A-83094 and A-14799, which are not adjacent on the path; account A-34114, which is not on the path, also sent from D-40018. The A-20636, A-28137 and A-85921 alerts have no device used by two or more of their path accounts. A-36729 (on the A-20636 path) shares device D-30793 with A-69026, which is not on that path.

What tells the alerts apart. As indicators they are alike: 6–8 distinct senders within one hour. The recorded relationships beyond the indicator differ. (a) Onward links: A-28137 has none. A-20636 and A-85921 have single-step paths to one account each, and some of their contributions have no onward link. A-10859 (3 links, branching to 2 end accounts), A-37573 (4 links) and A-83577 (5 links) have multi-step paths that every contribution feeds into. (b) Shared devices: only A-10859, A-37573 and A-83577 have a device shared by accounts on their paths. In the A-37573 case the alerted account and every intermediate account sent from one device, D-45880. (c) Amounts: in the recorded transfers, each onward transfer on the multi-step paths is slightly smaller than the one before it (for example 196000, 191000, 187500, 184000 on A-37573's first sequence, and 172000 down to 161500 on A-83577's). For interpretation: A-28137, and to a lesser degree A-20636 and A-85921, show nothing beyond the fan-in itself. A-37573, A-83577 and A-10859 combine fan-in with multi-step timing links and shared devices, which makes them the stronger candidates for review. These remain recorded relationships, not proof of fraud or common control.
Traceable provenance: each finding traces back to the transfer ids listed in its claims. Those ids come from the alert_contributions and onward_links tables of run run:5ce89f521e5e.

hypotheses.statement: A-37573's path accounts (A-37573, A-38045, A-93288, A-63022) may be operated by a single party: they all sent from D-45880, in quick succession, with slightly decreasing amounts. This would fit a layering pattern, but the data shows only device use and timing, not who controls the accounts or whether the same funds moved.

A-83577's sequence may be a relay pattern. D-40018 is shared by non-adjacent accounts A-83094 and A-14799, and also by off-path A-34114, which raises the possibility of a wider linked set. This is not established.
A-10859 and A-78340 may be controlled together, since both sent from D-79802. Not established.

A-28137's fan-in (small amounts, no onward links) and A-85921's (six identical 2500 transfers) could be ordinary collection activity, such as shared bills or a small merchant. The data cannot tell this apart from other explanations.

unresolved.question: What happened at the end accounts (A-92332, A-85287, A-36729, A-54215, A-39382, A-10758) after this dataset? The paths end only because there is no further qualifying transfer in this bounded replay.
Who controls or uses devices D-45880, D-79802 and D-40018? And what, if anything, connects A-34114 (D-40018) and A-69026 (D-30793) to the alerted paths?
Did the same funds actually move along these paths? Onward links record timing within 30 minutes, not where funds came from.
Are the contributing senders connected to each other in any way not recorded here, such as identity data or out-of-window activity?
